planting.note: Sow direct in spring into lean, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; tolerates dry, infertile coastal plain soils and needs no supplemental fertility.

directions: Coastal dogfennel forms an airy, finely divided clump of thread-like foliage topped with billowy, flat clusters of tiny white disc flowers from late summer into fall. It is distinct from the more common Eupatorium capillifolium in leaf texture and coastal plain habitat preference, favoring sandy pinelands and dune margins from North Carolina through Florida and west to Texas. Despite its weedy appearance, the profusion of small white blooms draws an outsized number of small native bees and other short-tongued pollinators during a season when few other nectar sources remain. Best used in informal native meadow plantings or naturalized coastal gardens where its loose, airy habit and drought tolerance can be appreciated without staking.
sources: Flora of the Southeastern United States (FSUS)
